unit.title: Physical uplinks: choose, investigate and hand over
unit.summary: Choose suitable media, compare both endpoint settings, investigate fresh error changes and finish a protected handover. Native topology/configuration/samples; no real equipment or shell.

tasks.title: Select a cable and matching interfaces for a long route
tasks.objective: A new 300 m route joins the access and distribution switches. The installed 80 m copper cable cannot reach it. Select a supplied cable and compatible interface profile at both ends to provide 1 Gb/s full duplex with error-free sample traffic. Keep the separate operations link unchanged.

introduction.introduction: You may skip or reopen this introduction. The separate worked example uses a 120 m route, a suitable 180 m OM2 cable and a short 100 m OM2 spare. Fill worked example prepares SX at both ends with the long-enough cable; Apply and sample traffic are separate actions. Try the short spare, inspect the failure and repair it. The example is separate and ungraded; it never replaces your assignment files or draft.

concepts.title: A link has two ends
concepts.text: A cable connects two interfaces. An interface is a connection point; a profile is one supplied media setting. Speed is data per second: 1 Gb/s means one gigabit each second; 100 Mb/s is one tenth of that rate. Both ends must support the same selected profile. Copper, multimode fiber and single-mode fiber are different choices; a matching connector name alone does not establish that a whole route is suitable.

concepts.title: Read the route and the supplied cable label
concepts.text: The route needs at least 300 m of cable. Compare that minimum with both the cable length and the profile reach table. A 200 m spare cannot span this route even though that length is within the SX profile.

concepts.title: Make and apply a configuration
concepts.text: Use the cable selector and both interface rows to prepare a change. Apply changes the simulated link. Inspect qualification and run sample traffic before Check work. No physical transceiver is inserted and no real network is contacted.

introduction.experiment_description: After the worked draft is applied, choose the short OM2 cable. Inspect why a cable can fit a profile yet still be too short for a route. Repair using a suitable cable/profile combination.

wrong.reason: The spare is shorter than the route.

partial.reason: Only one optical profile was changed.

hints: Compare the route minimum, the selected cable length and the profile limit. These are three different values.

Both interface profiles must match the chosen cable family. The supplied optical examples use Fixed 1 Gb/s full duplex; 1 Gb/s means one gigabit each second. Check the other end if qualification still fails.
For this 300 m route, a sufficiently long supplied OM2 cable with SX at both ends is one solution. A sufficiently long supplied OS2 cable with LX/LH at both ends is another.
tasks.worked_explanation: The route minimum rejects a short spare; the profile limit rejects a media/span outside its stated support. Compatible profiles and media at both ends then permit 1 Gb/s full-duplex operation in this model. Current service and independent traffic samples must both pass. Operations settings stay protected.
tasks.simulation_limits: Only supplied point-to-point interfaces, profiles, whole-metre cable spans, administrative settings and deterministic samples are modeled. Profile qualification is not carrier detection or optical/electrical certification. No IOS CLI, real packets, BER, DOM, cable insertion, MDIX, pause frames, timing/backoff, shared-media contention, STP or routed service. Copper minimum 1 m is a representation choice, not a physical standards minimum. Optical Auto and forced 1000BASE-T are outside this subset; do not generalize those omissions to all devices. Raw earlier readings are labeled authored samples and never grade evidence. Final applied outcomes are graded, not a claimed investigation click sequence or time-based handover availability.

tasks.title: Repair a link that is up but disagrees about duplex
tasks.objective: The access and distribution switches share a clean 20 m copper link. Users report poor delivery even though it is connected. Inspect both ends and compare their operating rate and duplex. Restore at least 100 Mb/s full duplex with no new modeled errors; keep the operations link unchanged.

introduction.introduction: You may skip or reopen this introduction. The separate example starts with both ends at Fixed 100 Mb/s half duplex. Fill worked example prepares Auto at both ends. Apply it, inspect the resulting full-duplex mode and run samples. Then change only one end to Fixed full duplex and investigate why agreement is lost. The example is separate and ungraded; it never replaces your assignment files or draft.

concepts.title: Connected does not always mean healthy
concepts.text: Rate is how fast the link operates. Duplex describes whether both ends can send at once. Full duplex supports simultaneous sending; both ends must agree. A link can be connected while the two ends disagree.

concepts.title: Compare configured and operating settings
concepts.text: Auto exchanges supported choices with another Auto end. In this deliberately modeled legacy 10/100 case, an Auto end can detect a Fixed peer rate but cannot learn that peer duplex and uses half duplex. Inspect the resulting operating settings rather than assuming Auto matches a Fixed full-duplex peer.

concepts.title: Use new evidence instead of blaming one old number
concepts.text: The supplied earlier CRC reading is an authored sample, not a diagnosis. Run current sample traffic and inspect changes. This model shows a deterministic half-side collision symptom for the supplied mismatch pattern; it does not predict real error rates or implement Ethernet backoff.

reading.note: Synthetic earlier reading, not a hardware capture or proof of the present fault

introduction.experiment_description: After both ends agree, set only the distribution end to Fixed 100 Mb/s full duplex. Inspect the operating settings and new sample errors, then repair both ends.

reading.note: Synthetic earlier reading, not a hardware capture or proof of the present fault

partial.reason: Auto still faces a Fixed full-duplex peer.

hints: Compare Auto/Fixed, rate and duplex on both ends, not only the connected status.
With this supplied legacy capability, Auto opposite Fixed full duplex can leave the Auto side at half duplex.
Auto on both ends or matching supported 100 Mb/s full-duplex settings on both ends are valid repairs. A rate mismatch is a different failure.
tasks.worked_explanation: Both Auto ends select their best shared advertised mode. Alternatively, both ends may use the same supported fixed rate and full duplex. An Auto/Fixed mismatch in this supplied legacy case can appear connected while one side uses half duplex; a fixed-rate mismatch instead prevents a common operating rate. Historical CRC alone proves neither cause.

tasks.title: Find a receive problem using fresh counter changes
tasks.objective: Both ends agree on 1 Gb/s full duplex, but transfer reports suggest lost frames. Use the current readings and two small traffic samples to determine whether errors are still occurring and restore clean delivery. Keep the required rate and the operations link unchanged. A zero total alone does not prove that the problem is repaired.

introduction.introduction: You may skip or reopen this introduction. The separate example has an every-fourth-frame teaching fault and starts at 96 offered, 72 received and 24 CRC errors at each end. Its worked draft selects a clean spare. Apply it, compare a new sample with the old baseline, then reselect the impaired cable and investigate the new increase. The example is separate and ungraded; it never replaces your assignment files or draft.

concepts.title: A total needs a baseline
concepts.text: A counter is a running total. One number does not tell you when the problem happened. Record the current value, send a known sample, then compare the new value with the baseline. Clearing this simulator counter is optional and changes only the starting total.

concepts.title: Keep historical and current evidence separate
concepts.text: The earlier reported reading is a synthetic source note. Current simulator counters are separate. In the worked example, both ends start with 96 offered, 72 received and 24 CRC errors from a supplied earlier sample. Compare new values with those baselines. Repairing a link does not automatically erase its older error totals.

concepts.title: Repeat a controlled test
concepts.text: Use sample sizes 12/18 and 24/15 in opposite directions. The separate worked example has an explicit every-fourth-frame impairment: a repeatable teaching fault, not a prediction of real errors. Investigate the assignment using its own readings and samples. After changing the cable, use new samples. Check work repeats traffic checks from its own sample counters, so clearing your displayed totals cannot hide the problem.

reading.note: Synthetic earlier reading, not a hardware capture or proof of the present fault

introduction.experiment_description: After using a clean spare, reselect the impaired cable. Compare a new sample with the baseline; clearing totals cannot prevent another increase. Repair using the other clean spare.

reading.note: Synthetic earlier reading, not a hardware capture or proof of the present fault

wrong.reason: The impaired cable remains and the rate was reduced below the task minimum.

partial.reason: The installed receive impairment remains even if historical totals are cleared.

hints: Compare operating modes first: both ends already agree. Then look at changes after fresh traffic.
With the installed impairment, clearing a counter just makes the next increase start at zero.
Either supplied inspected copper spare meets the route and rate requirements. Keep Auto at both 1 Gb/s-capable ends and verify that new samples add no receive errors.
tasks.worked_explanation: The original 32 CRC errors are history. Under the every-third-frame teaching fault, fresh 12/18 traffic adds 4 errors at the distribution receiver and 6 at the access receiver. After a valid clean spare is selected, all fresh sample frames arrive with no new modeled errors. Old counters may remain nonzero. Grading checks the current configuration against independent samples; it does not claim a click sequence proves investigative understanding.

tasks.title: Commission a replacement uplink and retire the old path
tasks.objective: Prepare the new 1200 m route using suitable supplied optical interfaces and cable. Verify 1 Gb/s full-duplex service with fresh samples, then stop both interfaces of the old uplink. Keep the independent operations link and its cable exactly as supplied. Finish with a healthy replacement and both old interfaces retired.

introduction.introduction: You may skip or reopen this introduction. The separate example uses an 800 m route and a suitable 1000 m OS2 cable. Its worked draft configures LX/LH at both ends and retires the old interfaces. Apply and verify it, then re-enable the old interfaces to see why the handover becomes incomplete. The example is separate and ungraded; it never replaces your assignment files or draft.

concepts.title: A handover includes what you leave behind
concepts.text: Restoring the new path is only part of the assignment. An old interface stays enabled until you explicitly stop it. This exercise models interface retirement and independent point-to-point links; it does not infer spanning-tree, routing or forwarding loops.

concepts.title: Choose a profile for this particular route
concepts.text: The supplied SX/OM2 profile supports up to 550 m and cannot qualify this 1200 m route. The supplied LX/LH with OS2 profile supports this span. These are specific teaching profiles, not a prediction about every optical product or a complete compatibility catalog.

concepts.title: Preserve a working neighbor
concepts.text: Use the new and old uplink rows for this task. Operations rows are a separate working link and are protected. Apply a complete draft, inspect the replacement, run samples, and confirm both old interfaces are stopped before Check work.

introduction.experiment_description: After preparing the new path, leave the old interfaces enabled. Check the resulting incomplete handover, then retire both old ends while preserving operations.

wrong.reason: The unrelated operations port was stopped.

partial.reason: The replacement works but both old interfaces remain enabled.

hints: The route is longer than the supplied SX/OM2 reach. Compare the provided optical profiles and cable lengths.
If service is healthy but completion still fails, check both old interfaces and the untouched operations rows.
LX/LH at both replacement ends with either sufficiently long supplied OS2 cable can qualify. Stop both old interfaces while keeping all operations settings and its cable unchanged.
tasks.worked_explanation: A suitable replacement must meet both the route minimum and the selected profile reach, have compatible ends and pass fresh samples. Turning up the replacement without stopping the old interfaces leaves the handover incomplete. Changing an unrelated working operations port is not an acceptable shortcut. No end-to-end routed service or real optical measurement is claimed.
